companyDescription: Sidewalk delivery robotics · ~2,000-robot fleet across 20 cities (44 cities/14 states incl. Diligent healthcare footprint) · Uber Eats/DoorDash/Nvidia/White Castle partnerships + Diligent Robotics healthcare acquisition · Q2 2026 earnings due Aug 6, 2026
priceNote: Self-fetched today (no live-prices.json cache yet). Closed Aug 3, 2026 at $5.65, up ~18% in the session as robotics names rallied broadly (Ouster +6%, Symbotic +4%) into Serve's Q2 print on Thursday Aug 6 — driven by options positioning and pre-earnings momentum, not new fundamental news. Still well below the $18.64 52-week high and now a step above the $4.32 low, but the sharp 2-day pump raises sell-the-news risk into a binary event just 2 days away.
summary: Serve Robotics reports Q2 2026 earnings after the close on Aug 6, 2026 — just 2 days out — with the stock up ~18% into the print on options positioning and a broad robotics-sector risk-on tape rather than fresh fundamentals. Consensus expects a $0.69/share GAAP loss (92% wider YoY) against ~$28M FY2026 revenue guidance (10x 2025), so the market is betting the ~2,000-robot fleet across 44 cities/14 states (with Diligent's hospital-robotics footprint) keeps scaling faster than losses widen. SERV's own earnings-day history stays genuinely mixed (+12.3% on the last beat, -3% on the last GAAP miss), and this cycle's unusually large pre-print rally adds a fresh sell-the-news risk on top of that. All 8 covering analysts still see meaningful upside (consensus $18.45, +226% from here, though Freedom Capital moved to Hold), anchored by real partnerships (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Nvidia, White Castle) and the Diligent healthcare diversification. Small-cap, pre-profitability, binary event in 48 hours — speculative sizing only, and chasing the current pump is not the preferred entry.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Serve reports after market close Aug 6, 2026. Consensus expects a $0.69/share GAAP loss (92% wider YoY) against ~$28M FY2026 revenue guidance (10x 2025). The stock's own earnings-day history is a coin flip — Q4 2025 results drove a +12.3% pop, but the May 2026 Q1 print fell over 3% on a GAAP net loss miss despite 578% YoY revenue growth. With the stock already up ~18% into the print, the market needs to see losses narrowing, not just faster top-line growth, or risk a sell-the-news reversal.

catalysts.name: Fleet at 2,000+ Robots, 44 Cities
catalysts.description: Fleet holds at ~2,000 robots across 20 core delivery cities, with the combined Serve + Diligent footprint spanning 44 cities in 14 states and nearing 2M cumulative deliveries. Focus has shifted from pure fleet growth to increasing revenue per robot — an operational proof point the market will scrutinize on the Aug 6 call.

catalysts.name: Diligent Robotics Healthcare Diversification
catalysts.description: The Diligent Robotics acquisition pushes Serve beyond food delivery into hospital service robotics — a diversification story that could re-rate the stock if it starts showing up materially in the revenue mix, alongside newer pilots like NoScrubs laundry delivery in LA.

risks: Stock is up ~18% in the two sessions into Aug 6 on options positioning and sector-wide risk-on tape (not new company news) — elevated sell-the-news risk if the print merely meets expectations
Consensus expects a $0.69/share GAAP loss, 92% wider YoY — the market is pricing 10x revenue growth to ~$28M, but May 2026's -3% reaction shows the loss line, not revenue growth, drives the stock
Own earnings-day history is genuinely mixed: +12.3% on the last beat (Mar 2026) but -3%+ on the last miss (May 2026)
Consensus target ($18.45) implies a ~226% move — even the low end of the analyst range ($13, +130%) requires a lot of good news; Freedom Capital Markets already moved to Hold ($18) from Buy

Competition from well-capitalized players (DoorDash's own robotics efforts) and volatile small-cap robotics peers (e.g., Richtech Robotics fell ~35% in H1 2026 on financial-restatement concerns) show how fast sentiment can turn in this niche

macroRisk.rateOutlook: The Fed held at 3.50–3.75% at the Jul 28–29, 2026 FOMC, though 3 members dissented in favor of a hike. The next decision is Sep 15–16, 2026, and remains a live meeting — the hawkish June dot plot put the median year-end 2026 projection at 3.8%, implying little room for cuts and a real chance of a hike depending on incoming CPI prints.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core inflation remains above target and long-end yields stay elevated — a real headwind for a pre-profitability small-cap that needs continued capital-market access to fund fleet expansion and integrate Diligent.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: As an unprofitable small-cap growth name, SERV is among the more rate-sensitive picks in this screen — higher-for-longer compresses the multiple the market pays for growth, compounding the existing execution-risk discount and the binary risk of Thursday's print.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — Fed held steady in July with hawkish dissents and a live September meeting; for a pre-profitability micro-cap like SERV, a hawkish September surprise would compound any post-earnings weakness from Aug 6.

Real growth story, but the market needs to see losses narrowing, not just revenue scaling, and this cycle's unusually large run-up raises sell-the-news risk on Aug 6.

catalystSpot.preRunup: SERV has historically shown limited pre-earnings drift, sitting flat into the print and reacting sharply on the actual numbers (especially the GAAP loss line). This cycle breaks that pattern: the stock rallied as much as 18% in the two sessions before Aug 6, alongside a broader robotics-sector risk-on move (Ouster +6%, Symbotic +4%) and options positioning — a materially bigger pre-event move than prior quarters, which raises sell-the-news risk if the print merely meets expectations.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 2 trading days before the print (Aug 3-4, 2026), vs. minimal historical drift

postWin.note: SERV's Q4 2025 results (reported Mar 11, 2026) drove a +12.31% pop — notable given the company's historical average earnings-day move is close to -4%, showing the market rewards a clean beat disproportionately for this name.

postLose.note: SERV's Q1 2026 results (reported May 7, 2026) fell over 3% despite 578% YoY revenue growth, because the GAAP net loss missed consensus and expansion spend raised cash-burn concerns — shows the market cares about the loss line, not just growth. With the stock already up ~18% pre-print this cycle, a repeat miss could see a sharper give-back than -3%.

spotSizing.reason: Pre-profitability micro-cap ($437M) with a genuinely mixed earnings-day track record, now compounded by an unusually large pre-earnings run-up — 3% sizing keeps real upside exposure while respecting both the binary loss-line risk and elevated sell-the-news risk.
